subject: Hosted API evaluation - next steps & quickstart
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation - next steps & quickstart

Hi Alexa —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the Hosted API evaluation: 

1) Recap of deployment options (high-level)
- Hosted API: fastest path for a POC, no infra to manage, pay-as-you-go. Good for early integration and user testing.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation (next step if you need steady high QPS or stricter SLAs).
- Private VPC / on-prem: for regulated data or customers that require customer-managed networking and KMS.

2) What we’ll provide for the Hosted POC
- Sandbox org + API key for your engineers.
- Quickstart guide (attached) and sample traffic template (attached) to mirror your expected patterns.
- Default endpoints that support streaming and chat-style flows.
- Default rate limits for Hosted (we can increase on request) — see Nikhil’s note below for details.

3) Ask from your side
- Expected peak and average QPS and tokens/day (you mentioned a mix of high-concurrency search and chat).
- Any data residency / compliance constraints we should know about for the POC.
- Preferred date/time for a 30–45m technical sync with Nikhil to walk through the quickstart and sample payloads.

Next steps I propose: I’ll have Nikhil spin up a sandbox org and share credentials + the quickstart steps. If the POC looks good after 2–3 weeks, we can discuss Dedicated sizing and an initial commitment.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-api-quickstart.pdf, acme-traffic-template.csv

—
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the follow-up and the quick demo. Hosted API sounds like the right starting point for our POC. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- Expected traffic: peak ~50 qps for search endpoints, average ~5 qps. Ballpark tokens: ~1M tokens/day during peak testing windows.
- Would like a separate staging/sandbox workspace for integration testing (not production).
- Can you confirm default per-minute request and token rate limits and burst behavior for Hosted? Also concurrent streaming connection limits.
- Procurement: we’d like an initial 3–month evaluation/POC. Who should our procurement team talk to for basic terms?

If you can get us a sandbox org and rate-limit details, we’ll schedule the technical sync for early next week (Tue/Wed morning PT looks best).

Thanks,

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>

Hi Alexa —

Thanks — happy to jump on the technical sync. Quick answers to your rate-limit / endpoint questions below; we can expand on this during the call and I can share a sandbox org and a short Postman collection.

Endpoints (Hosted API)
- Text generation (single-shot): POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Chat / streaming: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat (supports chunked streaming HTTP responses)
- Embeddings: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

Quickstart steps
1) I’ll create a sandbox org and generate an API key for your staging team.
2) Use the attached quickstart PDF or our docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/hosted-api/quickstart
3) Start with small batch sizes and enable streaming for low-latency chat flows.

Default Hosted rate limits (per-project, adjustable)
- Requests: 600 requests/minute (sustained) with a burst up to 1,200 requests/minute for short windows.
- Tokens: 100,000 tokens/minute (sustained) with short bursts available.
- Concurrent streaming connections: 50 by default.

Notes:
- If you expect sustained 50 qps with large token counts, we can temporarily raise limits for the POC — please share a sample hour of expected payload sizes from your traffic template and we’ll size appropriately.
- Billing is per-token for Hosted API; we’ll provide an estimate once we see your sample traffic.
- We can create a separate sandbox org (isolated) and provide a staging API key. That sounds like the right approach for you.

I’ll add a Postman collection and example payload to the sandbox org. Proposed tech sync times: Tue 7/14 or Wed 7/15, 9–11am PT. Which works for your engineers?

—
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
